Although it should _really_ tell you the name of what is actually deprecated here, at least. Otherwise it's going to be very confusing, figuring out what the warning is talking about in a given line.

Thanks, yep! I've seen that other warnings insert strings like "variable" or "method" so that the specifics are clearer to the user. I'm envisioning the final error message being something like:
```
The constant "PROPERTY_HINT_NODE_PATH_TO_EDITED_NODE" is deprecated. See its documentation for more information and alternatives.
```
It looks like there's a field to go alongside deprecated things that describes their replacement in the documentation structure. We should be able to pull those strings out and insert them in the warning message. So, for example, for [`Control.auto_translate`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_control.html#class-control-property-auto-translate), it could read:
```
The property "auto_translate" is deprecated: "Use Node.auto_translate_mode instead."
```
I don't think I saw that in my terminal output, so thanks for catching that! I'll have to take a look at it again and confirm it's working properly.

> Thanks, yep! I've seen that other warnings insert strings like "variable" or "method"

Ideally it would be nice if these strings (`"property"`, `"method"`, `"constant"`, etc.) already exist for another context. Otherwise, I think generalising it into `"identifier"` is okay, too. No need to split hair when the name in quotations makes the subject clear on its own.

> It looks like there's a field to go alongside deprecated things that describes their replacement in the documentation structure.

We... could, but it's more tricky than it looks. For displaying the actual deprecation message, ideally it would require exposing [a method that strips BBCode](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/78310#issue-comment-box), but also properly accounts for the custom BBCode tags that the class reference uses.

body:
I'm not sure, but perhaps the more correct term here is "symbol usage" or just "usage" rather than "identifier". As I understand it, identifiers are just words in the source code that denote a symbol. For example, if we had type aliases in the language, would it be appropriate to mark usages of a type alias that points to a deprecated class with this warning too?

"Deprecated identifier" sounds like we've deprecated some specific name everywhere, regardless of what it points to. For comparison:

* `CONFUSABLE_IDENTIFIER` - The symbol is not important, the problem is that the name itself contains visually confusing characters.
* `UNTYPED_DECLARATION`, `INFERRED_DECLARATION`, `CONFUSABLE_LOCAL_DECLARATION` - These warnings apply only to declarations, not to usages.
* `CONFUSABLE_LOCAL_USAGE` - This warning applies only to usages, not to declarations.

body:
It looks like that shouldn't be at all hard to implement (basically just duplicating the deprecated warning code) but I feel a bit split on whether this would make sense, user-wise. With deprecated APIs, there's more of an expectation (to me at least) that the API *is* going to disappear at some point, and that having it in the project will eventually be a liability. While an experimental API *may* change, it's less of a guarantee, and is for *incoming* functionality rather than *outgoing*.

Would you like to file a proposal for warnings about experimental APIs (or I can do so), that way the idea itself can be discussed more there?

Yes, it probably makes sense to discuss this in a separate proposal, without rushing things. I just meant that these are related fields, so implementing two warnings probably wouldn't add significant additional complexity.

As far as I know, sometimes users also try to avoid experimental APIs in production code if they don't want to rely on new features that are unstable or are subject to change or removal.

Note that different APIs, both deprecated and experimental, vary in their stability and irreplaceability. Just because a user wants to use one flagged API doesn't mean they want to use any flagged API. But we don't have a system for more granular configuration (something like parameterized warnings).

I've now added the deprecation message to the warning when available. BBCode is stripped out, but for things like methods and signals, the name of the symbol itself is kept. The one (possibly big) caveat to the current implementation is that class names are written the same way as standalone tags, so they get removed as well. So for example a deprecation string like:
```
Use a [Sprite2D] instead,[br] for better performance.
```
would get turned into
```
Use a   instead, for better performance.
```
I might be able to use `ClassDB::class_exists` to check the contents of a tag before completely removing it - will try that later today.

Thanks for the suggestion! It looks like that method is fairly tied into the C# generation (doing things such as replacing GDScript types with the C# equivalents) but I can use the general same approach as it for stripping out known BBCode tags 😄
